children: TOKYO, September 10 (Reuters) - Foreign investors remained netbuyers of Japanese stocks for the week ending on September 5, capital flows data showed on Thursday.    Foreigners bought a net 690.0 billion yen worth of shares inthe week through Sep. 5, after buying a net 35.9 billion yenin the week before that.    Japanese investors bought a net 111.9 billion yen of foreignbonds in the latest week after selling a net 824.0 billion yenthe week before.    Details of net investments were as follows (in billion yen):

FOREIGN INVESTMENT IN JAPAN:    (net)                                       stocks         bonds        bills    August 30 - September 5            +690.0        +449.6       -275.2     August 23 - August 29               +35.9r       +509.1        +16.6
JAPANESE INVESTMENT ABROAD:    (net; a minus sign indicates net selling and inflows of funds into Japan)

stocks         bonds        bills    August 30 - September 5            -481.6        +111.9       +103.8     August 23 - August 29               +35.8        -824.0         -9.7     August 2  - August 8               +927.4      +1,540.8r      -781.2

Notes:    - An "r" denotes a revised figure.    - Bonds include beneficiary certificates.    - Figures are based on contracts and are rounded.    - The MOF's capital flows data can be found in English at:    http://www.mof.go.jp/international_policy/reference/itn_transactions_in_securities/week.pdf
